s: Over 20 years, the global warming potential of methane is about how many times that of carbon dioxide?
x: Methane's GWP is about 84 times CO2 over 20 years and 28-34 times over 100 years.

s: According to the WHO, household air pollution causes about how many deaths every year?
x: The WHO puts household air pollution deaths at 3.2 million a year.

s: Kaziranga National Park has the world's largest population of which animal?
x: Kaziranga has the world's largest population of one-horned rhinoceros; its river dolphin is the Gangetic river dolphin.

s: Which institution conducted the DNA-based Synchronous All-India Population Estimation of elephants (2021–25) under Project Elephant?
x: The Wildlife Institute of India conducted the estimation under Project Elephant, which began in 1992.

s: The “elephant emergency” reported in February 2026 followed attacks in which group of States?
x: The elephant emergency followed attacks in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha. The other options combine States associated with elephant populations or other conflict regions, but they are not the group identified in this report.

s: According to the assessment of the elephant crisis in central India, approximately what share of elephants caused about half of the conflict casualties?
x: Less than 8% of elephants caused approximately 50% of conflict casualties. The other percentages do not represent the reported concentration of casualties.

s: As per the DNA-based elephant population estimation for 2021–25, what was India's elephant population?
x: The DNA-based estimate for 2021–25 was 22,446 elephants, against 27,312 in 2017 – a decline of about 18%, partly due to the new DNA method.

s: How long does elephant gestation last?
x: Elephant herds are matriarchal and gestation lasts 18–22 months.

s: How long is the elevated corridor inaugurated in Kaziranga National Park?
x: The elevated corridor is 34.5 km long; Kaziranga lies between the Brahmaputra and the Karbi Hills.

s: In which State is Anamalai Tiger Reserve, where the tiger census will use the M-STrIPES app, located?
x: Anamalai Tiger Reserve is in Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.

s: What is the IUCN status of the gharial (Gavialis gangeticus) of the Gandak River habitat?
x: Gavialis gangeticus is Critically Endangered.

s: Melghat Tiger Reserve is a stronghold of which bird?
x: Melghat is a stronghold of the forest owlet; Korku is its largest associated tribe.

s: Ratapani Tiger Reserve lies in Raisen and which other district of Madhya Pradesh?
x: Ratapani lies in Raisen and Sehore districts, with the Kolar River forming its western boundary.

s: How many dolphins did the Odisha Dolphin Census 2026 record?
x: The Odisha Dolphin Census 2026 recorded 765 dolphins.

s: Which organisation released 15 critically endangered Indian vultures at Melghat Tiger Reserve?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Bombay Natural History Society released 15 critically endangered Indian vultures at Melghat Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra. Wildlife Trust of India and the Bihar forest department were associated with gharial conservation efforts at the Gandak habitat.

s: Ratapani Tiger Reserve is to be renamed after which archaeologist, the discoverer of the Bhimbetka rock shelters?
x: The reserve is to be renamed after Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar, who discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters.

s: Which river is India's second-largest gharial habitat, with over 400 adult gharials recorded in 2025?
x: The Gandak is India's second-largest gharial habitat; the Chambal is the largest, with over 2,400 gharials.

s: According to NTCA data for 2025, which State recorded 55 tiger deaths?
x: Madhya Pradesh recorded 55 tiger deaths in 2025. Maharashtra recorded 38, while Kerala and Assam recorded 13 and 12 respectively; the national total was 166.

s: Which combination correctly matches the institutional history of tiger conservation in India?
o: NTCA was established in 2005 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; Project Tiger began in 1973
NTCA was established in 1973 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 2005; Project Tiger began in 1972
NTCA was established in 2005 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1973; Project Tiger began in 1972
NTCA was established in 1972 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 2005; Project Tiger began in 1973
x: The correct combination is NTCA established in 2005 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and Project Tiger beginning in 1973. The other options interchange the years or incorrectly attach the year 2005 to the Act.

s: On what does the dugong, called the 'sea cow', depend for food?
x: Dugong dugon is a seagrass-dependent herbivore found in India in the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay.

s: Which river is India's largest gharial habitat?
x: The Chambal is the largest gharial habitat (2,400+); the Gandak is the second-largest.

s: According to NTCA, how many tiger deaths were recorded in India in 2025?
x: NTCA recorded 166 tiger deaths in 2025 against 126 in 2024; Madhya Pradesh had 55.

s: Which was the first tiger reserve of Maharashtra?
x: Melghat, in the Gavilgarh Hills of the Satpuras, is Maharashtra's first tiger reserve.

s: What was India's elephant population in the 2017 count?
x: The 2017 count was 27,312; SAIEE 2021-25 found 22,446 (about 18% lower).

s: Kaziranga National Park lies between the Brahmaputra and which hills?
x: Kaziranga lies between the Brahmaputra and the Karbi (Mikir) Hills.

s: Which is the largest tribe of Melghat Tiger Reserve, Maharashtra?
x: Korku is the largest tribe of Melghat; Gawli and Gond also live there.

s: Where is Tamil Nadu's International Dugong Conservation Centre planned?
x: The EAC asked Tamil Nadu to revise the centre planned at Manora, Thanjavur.

s: In India, dugongs are mainly found in which areas?
o: Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay
Gulf of Khambhat and Konkan coast
x: Dugongs live in the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay (also Gulf of Kutch and A&N).

s: Goa became the second State to publish a state bird atlas. Which State was the first?
x: Goa became the second State after Kerala to publish a state bird atlas.

s: Why were seven rare galaxy frogs in Kerala's Western Ghats presumed dead?
x: The galaxy frogs vanished and were presumed dead because of disturbance by photo tourism.

s: What is the scientific name of the rare galaxy frog of the Western Ghats?
x: The galaxy frog is Melanobatrachus indicus; it lives under rotten logs and does not use vocal calls.

s: What is the IUCN status of the Chinese pangolin?
x: The Chinese pangolin is Critically Endangered, while the Indian pangolin is Endangered; both are in Schedule I and CITES Appendix I.

s: Which State became the first to declare a state microbe?
x: Kerala declared Bacillus subtilis, a Gram-positive, spore-forming probiotic, its state microbe.

s: The lion-tailed macaque, reported in the Anamalai Hills study, has which scientific name and IUCN status?
x: The lion-tailed macaque is Macaca silenus and is listed as Endangered by the IUCN. The other options alter either the scientific name or the conservation status.

s: Nagar Van Yojana, under which six urban forests were sanctioned in Telangana, is a scheme of which Union ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: Nagar Van Yojana is a scheme of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

s: What does the Indian Skimmer conservation project of BNHS and NMCG focus on protecting?
x: River sandbars are the Indian Skimmer's nesting sites.

s: How many JALAJ Livelihood Centres were inaugurated by the Union Jal Shakti Minister?
x: The minister inaugurated 25 JALAJ Livelihood Centres; 75 is the target.

s: Which microbe did Kerala declare as its state microbe?
x: Kerala, the first State to declare a state microbe, chose Bacillus subtilis.

s: The Sangtam Naga community, which resolved to protect pangolins, lives mainly in which State?
x: The Sangtam Nagas of Kiphire and Tuensang in Nagaland resolved to protect pangolins.

s: JALAJ Livelihood Centres are a joint initiative of Namami Gange and which institution?
x: JALAJ centres are run by Namami Gange with the Wildlife Institute of India (1982, Dehradun).

s: What is Chiraharitae?
o: Species of deer discovered in Madhya Pradesh
Long leaf plant discovered in Karnataka
Butterfly species discovered in Tamil Nadu
x: Glyptotermes chiraharitae is a termite species discovered in Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary, Kerala.

s: Siang is the Indian stretch of which river?
x: Siang is the Indian stretch of the Yarlung Tsangpo.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The ZSI is headquartered in Kolkata, not New Delhi. ZSI dates to 1916, BSI to 1890 and the Deep Ocean Mission to 2021.

s: The frogs Leptobrachium somani and L. mechuka were recorded from which State?
x: Both Leptobrachium species were recorded from Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Which newly reported mushroom represented the first record of the genus in India?
x: Hemileccinum indicum was reported from Bageshwar, Uttarakhand, and marked the first record of the genus in India. Parasola plicatilis is the Plaited Ink Cap, while Paracamptotheca alba and Hoya nagensis are a ginger and a wax plant respectively.

s: Which newly discovered species is an orchid recorded from Kanthalloor and Marayur in Idukki, Kerala?
x: Diplocentrum papillosum is the orchid discovered at Kanthalloor and Marayur in Idukki, Kerala. Dicliptera pakhalika, Impatiens nagorum and Arisaema siahaense are respectively a flowering plant from Telangana, a balsam from Nagaland and a cobra lily from Mizoram.

s: Which of the following statements about species discovered in February 2026 is incorrect?
o: Diplocentrum papillosum is an orchid recorded from Kanthalloor and Marayur in Idukki, Kerala.
Titanidiops kolhapurensis is a trapdoor spider found in the Kolhapur grasslands.
Polyrhachis garbhangensis is a spiny ant recorded from Garbhanga RF near Guwahati.
Lepidocampa sikkimensis is the second Diplura described by Indians and was recorded from Ravangla, Sikkim.
x: The incorrect statement is the fourth one. Lepidocampa sikkimensis was the first Diplura described by Indians, not the second; it was recorded from Ravangla, Sikkim.

s: What is Calamaria mizoramensis, recorded from Mizoram?
x: Calamaria mizoramensis is a non-venomous reed snake from Mizoram; Gegeneophis valmikii is a caecilian from Maharashtra.

s: Which newly recorded squat lobster was found near Minicoy at about 360 metres, in connection with Samudrayaan and the Deep Ocean Mission?
x: Leiogalathea samudragiri is the squat lobster found near Minicoy at about 360 metres. Alpheus madhusoodanai is a pistol shrimp from the Kochi backwaters, while Galathea balasubramaniani is a reef crab from Agatti.

s: Glyptotermes chiraharitae, whose name comes from the Sanskrit word for 'evergreen', is a new species of which kind?
x: Glyptotermes chiraharitae is a dampwood termite; 'chiraharita' means evergreen.

s: In which State was the termite Glyptotermes chiraharitae discovered?
x: It was found in the Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary (Kakkayam), Kozhikode, Kerala.

s: What kind of animal is Gegeneophis valmikii, reported from the northern Western Ghats of Maharashtra?
x: Gegeneophis valmikii is a caecilian, a limbless amphibian.

s: Dicliptera pakhalika, a new flowering plant described by the Botanical Survey of India, was found in which protected area?
x: Dicliptera pakhalika was found in Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary, Warangal, Telangana.

s: Impatiens nagorum, a new balsam named after the Naga tribes, was found in which State?
x: Impatiens nagorum was found in Fakim Wildlife Sanctuary, Kiphire, Nagaland.

s: Indiafonte bijoyi, a copepod of a new genus, was found in which lagoon?
x: Indiafonte bijoyi was found in Kavaratti Lagoon, Lakshadweep.

s: What is Alpheus madhusoodanai, reported from the Kochi backwaters?
x: Alpheus madhusoodanai is a new pistol shrimp from the Kochi backwaters.

s: Galathea balasubramaniani, a tiny reef crab, was found at which island of Lakshadweep?
x: The 3 mm reef crab Galathea balasubramaniani was found at Agatti.

s: Arisaema siahaense, a new cobra lily, was found in which State?
x: Arisaema siahaense was found at Siaha, Mizoram.

s: Where was the bolete mushroom Hemileccinum indicum, the first of its genus in India, found?
x: Hemileccinum indicum was found in Bageshwar, Uttarakhand.

s: Lepidagathis konkanensis, a new wildflower, was found in which district?
x: Lepidagathis konkanensis was found in Ratnagiri, Konkan.

The Parvati–Arga Bird Sanctuary was notified as an Eco-Sensitive Zone in which State?

s: About how much of the Great Nicobar Island Project area was allegedly in prohibited zones under the ICRZ Notification 2019?
x: About 700 ha were allegedly in ICRZ 2019 prohibited zones, alongside concerns over 130 sq km of rainforest.

s: Which tribes are associated with the Great Nicobar Island Project area?
x: The Shompen and Nicobarese are the tribes associated with the project.

s: Under which Article did Tamil Nadu file its suit against Karnataka in the Pennaiyar River dispute?
x: Tamil Nadu invoked Article 131; the Supreme Court directed the Centre to set up a tribunal within one month.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Valley of Flowers and Lohit Valley?
o: The fire at Valley of Flowers National Park in Chamoli lasted five days
The Lohit River is a tributary of the Ganga
Valley of Flowers is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Nanda Devi National Park
Valley of Flowers was discovered in 1931 by Frank S. Smythe
x: The Lohit is a tributary of the Brahmaputra, not the Ganga.

s: In which year did Bannerghatta National Park, about 22 km south of Bengaluru, become a national park?
x: Bannerghatta, in the Anekal hills, was a reserved forest in 1970 and became a national park in 1974.

s: The Pangolakha range forms part of the boundary between Sikkim and which country?
x: The Pangolakha range forms part of the Sikkim–Bhutan boundary.

s: The Aravalli range is nearly how old?
x: The Aravallis are nearly two billion years old, making them India's oldest range; they run about 670–692 km from Gujarat to Delhi.

s: In its order of 16 February 2026, what did the NGT decide on the environmental clearance for the Great Nicobar Island Project?
o: Referred it to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
x: The NGT upheld the environmental clearance, noting that adequate safeguards were in place.

s: Which wildlife sanctuary was renamed Kerala's first butterfly sanctuary?
x: Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary in Kannur district was renamed Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary and became Kerala's first butterfly sanctuary. Kottiyoor and Brahmagiri are bordering wildlife sanctuaries, while Kumbhalgarh is in Rajasthan.

s: Protection of the Aravallis has been treated as part of the case law of which Article?
x: Protection of the Aravallis is part of Article 21 jurisprudence, not Article 14.

s: In January 2026, the Central Empowered Committee recommended restoring the Bannerghatta Eco-Sensitive Zone to its extent of which year?
x: The CEC recommended restoring the ESZ to its 2016 extent and scrapping the reduced 2020 notification.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Aravallis?
o: A restoration pilot covered four villages around Gurugram.
About 43% of households in the study depend on Aravalli forests for fodder, fuelwood and medicinal plants.
The range is nearly two billion years old.
Guru Shikhar, the highest peak of the range, is in Gujarat.
x: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) is at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, not Gujarat; the restoration-study facts are correct.

s: Under the Supreme Court's November 2025 uniform definition, only hills above what elevation are treated as Aravallis?
x: The uniform threshold is above 100 m; fresh mining leases were paused in Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

s: Which of the following about the Supreme Court's Aravalli framework is INCORRECT?
o: The 100-metre rule excludes more than 90% of the landscape.
A total ban was not imposed, as total bans can fuel illegal mining.
The Management Plan for Sustainable Mining covers only the 5-km green buffer.
The 5-km green buffer belongs to the Aravalli Green Wall Project.
x: The Management Plan for Sustainable Mining is to be prepared for the entire Aravalli range, not only the 5-km buffer.

s: Which of the following Aravalli protection milestones is correctly matched?
o: May 2024 – Halt on new mining leases
November 2025 – Supreme Court ban on mining in Gurugram, Faridabad and Mewat
x: New mining leases were halted in May 2024. The 2009 milestone was the mining ban in Gurugram, Faridabad and Mewat, and November 2025 brought the uniform 100-metre definition.

s: Where is Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary, where a forest fire was reported, located?
x: The fire occurred in Pangolakha in East Sikkim near the India–China border, at about 13,000 feet.

s: Which authority issued a show-cause notice to the Narmada Valley Development Authority over Bargi Dam?
x: The National Dam Safety Authority issued the show-cause notice to the Narmada Valley Development Authority over Bargi Dam. The Central Empowered Committee dealt with the Bannerghatta Eco-Sensitive Zone, while NMCG and the Expert Appraisal Committee were associated with other environmental matters.

s: What do butterflies mainly absorb by mud or soil puddling?
x: Mud puddling lets butterflies absorb minerals and salts, not nectar.

s: The Lohit, whose valley saw forest fires fought by IAF aerial water bombing, is a tributary of which river?
x: The Lohit is a Brahmaputra tributary, not a Ganga tributary.

s: After whom is Rajaji National Park in Uttarakhand named?
x: Rajaji NP is named after C. Rajagopalachari.

s: Protests by about 20,000 people were held against which proposed port in Palghar district, Maharashtra?
x: About 20,000 people protested against the Vadhavan Port in Palghar, Maharashtra.

s: Bargi Dam, which received a safety-related notice, is built on which river?
x: Bargi Dam is built on the Narmada River.

s: Which distinction is associated with the 260-metre Tehri Dam?
o: It is the tallest dam in India
It is the first completed dam on the Narmada
It is the deepest reservoir in India
It is the only earth and rock-fill dam in India
x: The 260-metre Tehri Dam is the tallest dam in India. The first completed dam on the Narmada refers to Bargi Dam, while the facts do not identify Tehri as India’s deepest reservoir or its only earth and rock-fill dam.

s: The Sawalkot Mega Hydroelectric Project, associated with India's exit from the Indus Waters Treaty, is being developed on which river in which district?
o: Rapti in Balrampur district, Uttar Pradesh
x: The Sawalkot Mega Hydroelectric Project is located on the Chenab in Ramban district, J&K. The Ravi–Pathankot association belongs to the Shahpur Kandi project, while Pennaiyar and Rapti are associated with separate river-related developments.

s: In which year was the Shahpur Kandi Project declared a national project?
x: Shahpur Kandi became a national project in 2008, with costs shared 80% by Punjab and 20% by the Centre.

s: Where does the Jhelum, into which Dal Lake drains, originate?
x: The Jhelum originates at Verinag, not Srinagar.

s: Under which rulers was Futala (Telangkhedi) Lake, a man-made lake in Nagpur, built in the 18th century?
x: Futala Lake is a man-made lake in Nagpur built under Bhonsle rule in the 18th century.

s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960, which rivers were given to India?
x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej went to India; the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab went to Pakistan.

s: On which river is the Shahpur Kandi project in Pathankot built?
x: Shahpur Kandi is on the Ravi in Pathankot; it became a national project in 2008.

s: On which river is Tehri Dam, India's tallest dam, built?
x: The 260 m Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi and is run by THDC India.

s: Vadhavan Port in Palghar is being developed by JNPA and which other body?
x: Vadhavan Port is a JNPA and Maharashtra Maritime Board project, about 140 km north of Mumbai.

s: Where is Piton de la Fournaise, a basaltic shield volcano in the news, located?
x: Piton de la Fournaise is a basaltic shield volcano on Réunion Island.

s: Mayon volcano, whose eruption led to the evacuation of about 3,000 people, is in which Philippine province?
x: Mayon volcano is in Albay province on Luzon island in the Philippines.

s: To which country were Karnataka's GI products Nanjangud Rasabale banana, Mysuru betel leaves and Indi lemon exported?
x: The three Karnataka GI products were exported to Maldives.

s: After five more products received GI tags, what was Tamil Nadu's total GI count?
x: Tamil Nadu's GI count rose to 74 after five products received GI tags.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Mount Bur Ni Telong is part of the Atlantic Ring of Fire.
Mount Bur Ni Telong is in Aceh Province, Sumatra.
The Red Sea lies between Africa and Arabia.
Mount Bur Ni Telong is a 2,624 m stratovolcano.
x: Bur Ni Telong is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, not an Atlantic one; the other statements are correct.

s: From which district is Kavindapadi nattu sakkarai, a GI-tagged product of Tamil Nadu?
x: Kavindapadi nattu sakkarai is from Erode; Woraiyur sari is from Tiruchi and Ambasamudram Choppu Saman from Tirunelveli.

s: What measure did Saudi Arabia introduce for Red Sea coastal tourism from January 2026?
o: A fertiliser-control programme to prevent eutrophication
An alert-level increase and evacuation programme
A ballistic-missile monitoring system and port restrictions
Mandatory rules for beach operators and a digital coastal guide
x: Saudi Arabia introduced mandatory rules for beach operators along with a digital coastal guide from January 2026. The other options combine details associated with volcano alerts, the Sea of Japan missile event, and phosphorus pollution.

s: Which of the following places in the news is wrongly matched?
o: Strait of Hormuz – Diego Garcia and the British Indian Ocean Territory
Lake Victoria – algal bloom and eutrophication
Chagos Islands – Diego Garcia and the British Indian Ocean Territory
x: The Strait of Hormuz carries about 20% of global crude; Diego Garcia and the BIOT relate to the Chagos Islands.

s: For how many years is a Geographical Indication registration in India valid?
x: A GI registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely.

s: Nagauri Ashwagandha became which agricultural GI of Rajasthan after Sojat Mehndi?
x: Nagauri Ashwagandha became Rajasthan's second agricultural GI, after Sojat Mehndi.

s: Through which strait does the Sea of Japan connect to the Pacific Ocean?
x: The Sea of Japan reaches the Pacific through the Tsugaru Strait; Tsushima leads to the East China Sea and Kanmon to the Inland Sea.

s: In which direction from Port Blair does Barren Island, India's only active volcano, lie at about 135 km?
x: Barren Island lies about 135 km north-east of Port Blair, not south-east.

s: The Gulf of Mannar was declared India's first marine biosphere reserve in which year?
x: The Gulf of Mannar became India's first marine biosphere reserve in 1989. The other years refer to different environmental initiatives and designations, not this milestone.

s: Shiveluch, the Russian stratovolcano that erupted recently, is known for which kind of magma?
x: Shiveluch is a stratovolcano with super-hydrous magma; its eruption sent ash up to about 9,000 m.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mount Bur Ni Telong volcano alert?
o: The volcano is in Bener Meriah Regency, Aceh Province.
Indonesia reduced the alert level after a surge in seismic activity.
x: Indonesia raised, not reduced, the alert level and began evacuations.

s: North Korea fired a ballistic missile towards which water body?
x: The missile was fired towards the Sea of Japan, also known as the East Sea. The East China Sea, Okhotsk Sea and Pacific Ocean are connected water bodies listed in relation to the Sea of Japan, but they were not the stated direction of this missile launch.

s: The Sea of Japan (East Sea) is bounded by which of the following countries?
o: Japan, North Korea, South Korea and China
Japan, Russia, China and South Korea
Japan, Russia, North Korea and South Korea
Russia, North Korea, South Korea and China
x: The Sea of Japan is bounded by Japan, Russia, North Korea and South Korea. The tempting alternatives are incorrect because they replace one of these four countries with China.

s: Under which body and ministry does the GI Registry function?
o: DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry
NABARD under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DPIIT under the Ministry of Agriculture
Tamil Nadu State Agricultural Marketing Board under DPIIT
x: The GI Registry is under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry. NABARD and the Tamil Nadu State Agricultural Marketing Board were associated with product applications, not the GI Registry.

s: Lake Victoria, which turned green due to an algal bloom, is the source of which river?
x: Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, is the source of the White Nile.

s: Woraiyur cotton sari, which received a GI tag, is from which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: Woraiyur cotton sari is from Tiruchi.

s: Which channel separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep?
x: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep.

s: Which channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives?
x: The Eight Degree Channel lies between Minicoy and the Maldives.

s: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and which territory?
x: The Strait of Hormuz, carrying about 20% of global crude, lies between Iran and Oman's Musandam.

s: Vaan Island, with an artificial reef project, is off which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: Vaan Island is in the Gulf of Mannar off Thoothukudi.

s: Ambasamudram Choppu Saman, a new GI product of Tamil Nadu, is from which district?
x: Ambasamudram Choppu Saman is from Tirunelveli.
